intro: Welcome to Çorum Museum, in Çorum province, founded in 1968. This is the central museum for the Hattusa, Alacahöyük and Şapinuwa excavations, and it holds what they produced: Hittite cuneiform tablets, seals and bull figurines.
history: The museum was founded in 1968 and later moved into the old Çorum hospital. Today it is the central collection for the Hattusa, Alacahöyük, Şapinuwa and Ortaköy excavations, gathering the cuneiform tablets, seals and cult objects of the Hittite world. After them, in the same sequence, come the region's Phrygian, Roman and Byzantine layers.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Hittite tablets, the finds from Alacahöyük, the seal collection and the ethnography section.
facts: Did you know? The tens of thousands of tablets found at Hattusa made it possible to decipher Hittite, and they yielded the earliest written record of any Indo-European language. The museum is the central collection for the Hattusa and Alacahöyük excavations, and it is here that their Hittite seals and tablets are gathered.
outro: This brings our tour of Çorum Museum to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
